> 蒙。亨。匪我求童蒙，童蒙求我。

Hexagram four is about teaching, and almost every modern Chinese reader takes its name to mean ignorance.

說文 does not: 蒙，王女也 — 王女 is a plant, dodder, a climbing thread that covers what it grows on. From that, 蒙 is covering, being covered over.

So 蒙's original sense is not "stupid." It is "covered up."

Which changes the entire hexagram, because a light that is covered is still a light. It can be uncovered. A thing that is dark by nature cannot.

## 童 is unmarked, not childish

童's older use has two layers: 說文 男有罪曰奴，奴曰童 — the form contains 辛, the instrument of punishment, so the earliest sense is tied to servitude. Later it becomes the word for a boy not yet capped.

蒙卦's 童蒙 takes the second layer: a mind not yet marked by acquired learning.

童 here is not a put-down. It is: the original is not yet dispersed.

## 瀆 is a ditch

說文: 瀆，溝也 — a ditch, a drain. The sense "to treat lightly, to profane" belongs to a different character, 嬻.

So 初筮告，再三瀆 is not "asking too many questions." It is asking lightly.

The first asking is answered. The third and fourth are not more inquiry — they are the same question handled carelessly, which is no longer a question.

## 說 means 脫

初六 用說桎梏.

說 here is 脫 — to be released. 經典釋文 gives the reading 吐活反 precisely to prevent the other one.

Without this, the line reads as "use persuasion on people wearing shackles," which is nonsense.

## 刑 read as 型

利用刑人 — two readings exist: punishment, or model.

This book takes "model," and the reason is the next clause: 用說桎梏, whose purpose is release.

If 刑 meant punishment, the two halves of the line would contradict each other. A line that ends in setting someone free does not begin with shackling him.

## 金夫 is not a rich man

六三 見金夫，不有躬.

Wang Bi: 金夫，謂二也 — the "gold man" is line two, and 金 stands for the hard and firm. 孔穎達 agrees: 金夫，謂九二剛陽之夫.

So it is "the hard man," not "the man with money." This is one of the most commonly reversed glosses in modern commentaries, and it reverses the line's meaning entirely: the woman sees strength and loses her own bearing — not wealth.

## 養正

蒙以養正，聖功也.

The purpose of instruction is not to fill someone with information. It is to keep the original uprightness alive while the covering is removed.

Which is the sentence that makes this hexagram unlike a chapter on education. Nothing is being installed. Something already there is being uncovered, and the risk is that the uncovering damages it.

## 匪我求童蒙，童蒙求我

Not I seeking the child, but the child seeking me.

The direction of the request is the hexagram's condition. Instruction that begins from the teacher's initiative arrives before the covering has been noticed — and what arrives before the question is not instruction, it is decoration.

## A test

Take something you are trying to teach — a person, a team, a reader. Ask whether the covering has been noticed yet. If not, everything you say will be received as information, and information is what the covering is made of.
